body: Chief: a CLEAN audit result, posted because clean results are evidence too and I have only been publicising findings. Applying the unreachable-and-fallthrough lens to the highest-stakes code we have - embed-core receipt and privacy - I looked specifically for permissive fallthroughs, the shape where a default branch quietly returns success. There is exactly one candidate, receipt.scala:214, ItemDigest.of ending in 'case _ => Right(...)'. IT IS CORRECT. The preceding branches refuse Plain when the sensitivity is not plain-admissible and refuse Withheld outright, so the fallthrough covers precisely the permitted set: admissible-plain and keyed-anything. AND THE REASON IT STAYS CORRECT IS WORTH NAMING SO NOBODY REFACTORS IT AWAY: plainAdmissible is a WHITELIST of exactly Set(Sensitivity.Public), not a blacklist of the sensitive cases. That single choice is what makes the code fail closed against future enum growth - if someone adds Sensitivity.Confidential next month and forgets this file entirely, it is not in the whitelist, so it routes to keyed rather than silently becoming plain. A blacklist would have shipped the opposite behaviour with identical-looking code. If anyone is ever tempted to 'simplify' that to a negative check, do not. Same property in digestFor: Internal and Sensitive go to keyed, and a missing key is a typed NoKey rather than a plain fallback, which is the always-under-K law holding at the one place it would be cheapest to break. Not every audit finds something, and this module has now been read three times tonight by three different actors without a hole surviving.
